{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-pa-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"9f9616bee6223de8fce2d17ae89dbf521c3a3663d6d7423d07b9bdc2de5e2908","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-pa-class-c:lineage:47","source_registry_sha256":"643bc755bc144bbb64c82e5b21691c27918519b2f96f9b0ff96b63899c04fddb","source_liveness_sha256":"d125293461efac0b369397a252e58fe1686ca24cdc89a306e2ea205c1feddb7c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Highways and parking","heading":"C — Highways and parking","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Highways and parking

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Before entering a highway, avoid mistaking the exit ramp for the entrance; watch ONE WAY, WRONG WAY and DO NOT ENTER signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
A green HIGHWAY ENTRANCE sign may identify an entrance ramp, but is not always present. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
A white edge line on the right and yellow on the left indicate the proper direction of travel on the ramp. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
In a shared weaving lane, an entering driver yields to the exiting driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Use an acceleration lane to build toward traffic speed, checking the side mirror and looking over the shoulder for a gap. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
Move into the exit lane early and slow only after entering that lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
If the exit is missed, use the next exit rather than stopping, reversing, crossing multiple lanes suddenly or crossing the median. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
Exit-ramp warning signs indicate the maximum safe ramp speed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
At 65 mph, a vehicle covers almost 100 feet per second. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
When passing on a highway, change only one lane at a time and signal each lane change well ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
A through driver may help a highway entrant by changing lanes courteously, but must first verify space is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
Highway hypnosis develops when prolonged staring replaces scanning ahead, behind and around the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
Along a curb, park as close as possible and no farther than 12 inches away. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A01
Without a curb, park as far off the roadway as possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A01
When roadway parking is necessary, use hazard flashers, allow passing room and remain visible for at least 500 feet in both directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A01
Park facing the direction of traffic and secure the vehicle against movement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A01
When parking, set the parking brake and select Park for an automatic transmission, or Reverse or First for a manual. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A01
For downhill parking with a curb, turn the wheels fully right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A01
For uphill parking with a curb, turn the wheels left. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A01
On a hill without a curb, point the wheels right whether facing uphill or downhill. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0056]

Misconceptions: a missed exit requires continuing to the next; highway entrants yield even when through drivers courteously make room; parking restrictions retain emergency and police-direction exceptions.
Mnemonics: choose the ramp, merge safely, exit deliberately and secure the parked vehicle.
Glossary: a weaving lane is shared by entering and exiting traffic; highway hypnosis is loss of active scanning; double parking occupies the roadway beside an already parked vehicle.
Dynamic facts: no officeholder, local answer or time-varying value is asserted; handbook edition currency is tracked as source debt in the authority part.
